title: Reining in Complexity: Data Science & Future of AI/ML Businesses

reader_summary.headline: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6&Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6&Z podcast. For this week's episode, we have one of our hallway-style conversations. Our guest, even questions our view of software eating the world, or rather, ask, what happens when software is everywhere, what comes next?

thesis: The conversation explores the debate between data warehouse maximalists who believe SQL can handle all data needs versus 'Hadoop refugees' who argue that sophisticated computation requires Python and R. The speakers identify 'shadow data management' as a pernicious problem where organizations bypass expensive, slow enterprise databases by using file shares and scripts, effectively allowing data science to eat this unmanaged data. They argue that while SQL is suitable for business data analytics, it is inadequate for hardcore statistics and complex problem domains, suggesting a heterogeneous landscape where different tools serve distinct purposes rather than a single convergence.
